title: Scientific Interoperability Incubator for Pan-NIH Resources (SIIPR)
bodyHtml:
Last week, a voluntary coalition of NIH resource builders, funders, users, & partners convened at the Scientific Interoperability Incubator for Pan-NIH Resources (SIIPR) to determine how our resources can do more together than alone. This 75+ person event served as a call to action to develop a new shared model for scientific interoperability, across the science layer and data layer. The outcome of this meeting was develop several pilot projects, working groups, and outputs such as white papers, products, and new standards.

As these discussions progressed over the two day event, three major topic areas emerged:

  1. Developing MCP gateway that could connect different NIH resources, MCP servers, APIs, Knowledge Graphs, and tools.
  2. Create an NIH gene set registry, or gene set standard, since gene sets are widely used but have barriers due to poor naming conventions, no mechanism to track gene set context, unknown quality, and often lack provenance at scale.
  3. Knowledge Graph integration via modules, where NIH KGs could publish standardized modules or assertions that can be reused across systems.

Post-meeting, our immediate next step is working towards an MCP server for NIH resources. Please be on the look out for additional readouts, which will be published soon. We'd like to invite those interested in collaborating to join our Coalition of the Willing by contacting the Knowledge Center at help@cfdeknowledge.org.

If you are interested in learning more about this event and are attending ISMB, join Julie Jurgens as she presents at the BOSC track on July 15 from 2:40 - 3:00 or during her poster sessions on July 15-16th.
